Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context:
A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by creating a dated document, recording the subject, verifying required fields, obtaining sign-off, and archiving the record in the standard index for retention.

2) What occurred:
The actor prepared a dated request document to modify the building's inspection record without completing the mandated safety verification step.
The actor altered the compliance status field to show a passed result without performing the required physical inspection, leaving the actual inspection check unverified.
The actor added a false sign-off field attributed to a named inspector account, bypassing the authorization verification check for that sign-off.
The actor filed the modified record in the archive index on the record date, with the original violation documentation field left unverified as superseded.
The actor submitted a payment receipt document referencing the account transaction ID, with the payment purpose field unverified against the official fee schedule.

3) Materials/access observed:
Document: inspection record (dated, modified status field)
Field: compliance status (altered from "failed" to "passed")
Field: inspector sign-off (false attribution)
Document: payment receipt (dated, referencing account transaction)
Channel: records archive index (modified filing entry)
Account: named inspector account (used for false sign-off)
Date: record modification date (matching the falsified inspection date)

4) Indicators & artifacts:
Mismatch between the recorded inspection date and the absence of physical inspection artifacts in the work log.
Payment transaction recorded outside the official fee schedule range for standard inspections.
Inspector sign-off timestamp not matching the named account's authenticated activity log for that period.
Original violation documentation marked superseded without a documented correction or appeal process reference.
Archive filing metadata showing the record was edited after initial submission, with no audit trail of the modification.
The actor used the records office access credentials to file the modified document, with the access log showing the session duration inconsistent with standard filing procedures.
